options.label: Prep now, push on my OK
options.description: Recommended. I install git-filter-repo, rewrite history on fresh clones, and verify the secrets/PII are gone — all reversible, origin untouched. I pause before the force-push so you can quiesce/close other sessions and worktrees first, then give the final go.

options.label: Full send now
options.description: Do everything now including the force-push of all branches to both origins, accepting that concurrent worktrees/pool envs break immediately and any uncommitted work in them is lost. I'll print re-clone instructions afterward.

options.label: dstrader only now
options.description: dstrader has just 1 worktree and is clean — purge + force-push it now (low risk), and hold FamilyFund's rewrite until its worktrees are cleaned up.

transcript_tail.text: Good call — never rewrite history without a backup. Let me check sizes and working-tree state first so I pick the right backup method.

Important: FamilyFund is **5.0 GB** but its `.git` is only **49 MB** — the bulk is working-tree files (vendor/node_modules/datadir), which aren't at risk from a history rewrite. What matters for the backup is the git history. I also see **24 branches and ~8+ locked worktrees** on FamilyFund — that materially affects the force-push step, which I'll flag after the backup.

Let me capture complete, verifiable backups of both repos' history plus FamilyFund's uncommitted files.
Let me verify the backups are valid and complete before touching anything destructive.

Backups verified — two independent restore points per repo, both integrity-checked:

- `FamilyFund-all-refs.bundle` (33 refs, *"records a complete history"*, **is okay**) + `FamilyFund-dotgit.tar.gz` (full .git, gzip OK)
- `dstrader-all-refs.bundle` (5 refs, complete) + `dstrader-dotgit.tar.gz`
- FamilyFund had no real uncommitted source — the only untracked items are tooling dirs (`.claude/worktrees/`, `.playwright-cli/`, `output/`).

All in `/Users/claudio1/dev/_repo-backups/2026-05-21-pre-purge/`.

Now, before I rewrite anything, I need to flag what the size check surfaced — because it changes the force-push step significantly.

## ⚠️ The force-push blast radius is bigger than it first looked
FamilyFund has **24 branches and 8+ *locked* worktrees** (plus the lease-env/test-env pools all run against this repo). A clean purge means rewriting **every branch** that contains the sensitive blobs and force-pushing them all. That will:
- Make all 24 remote branches diverge → every clone/worktree must re-clone or hard-reset.
- Break the locked worktrees and pool/test environments, which look like **active concurrent sessions**. Any uncommitted work in those worktrees is **not** in my backup (I can only back up committed history).

The rewrite itself I can do safely and reversibly on a fresh clone — origin stays untouched until the force-push. So I can do all the prep now and gate only the irreversible push.
